title: Errors: 402 and 413 fall through to the generic APIError, though both are documented and both are actionable
body:
## Summary

`APIError.fromResponse` maps seven statuses to typed subclasses and sends everything
else to the base `APIError`, so `402`, `409` and `413` arrive untyped. `402` is the
one worth acting on: it is how a metered API reports that a balance has run out, and
a caller that cannot match on it cannot branch to "top up" or "fall back" without
string-matching or inspecting `status` by hand.

## What happens

```js
import { APIError } from '@typesafe-ai/sdk'

APIError.fromResponse(400, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'BadRequestError'
APIError.fromResponse(401, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'AuthenticationError'
APIError.fromResponse(402, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'APIError'   <-
APIError.fromResponse(403, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'PermissionDeniedError'
APIError.fromResponse(404, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'NotFoundError'
APIError.fromResponse(409, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'APIError'   <-
APIError.fromResponse(413, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'APIError'   <-
APIError.fromResponse(422, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'UnprocessableEntityError'
APIError.fromResponse(429, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'RateLimitError'
APIError.fromResponse(500, {}, new Headers()).constructor.name // 'InternalServerError'
```

The exported classes are `APIError`, `BadRequestError`, `AuthenticationError`,
`PermissionDeniedError`, `NotFoundError`, `RateLimitError`, `UnprocessableEntityError`,
`InternalServerError` and the connection/timeout/abort trio — there is no
`PaymentRequiredError` or `PayloadTooLargeError`.

## Why it matters

- **`402` is a normal operating condition for a metered API, not an edge case.** It
  is the signal that a prepaid balance or invoice has run out. A wrapper that wants
  to prompt for billing, or fall back to a local model, has to special-case a bare
  number today. Every other actionable failure mode already has a class.
- **`413` is reachable from documented limits.** The models page states a 64k token
  budget per request, with 32k for `state` plus the longest question. Exceeding it is
  a caller-side mistake with an obvious fix (batch or truncate), which is exactly
  what a typed error lets a wrapper do automatically.
- **The API reference documents both**, so a caller reading the docs expects to be
  able to catch them by type.

## Suggested fix

```ts
export class PaymentRequiredError extends APIError {}
export class ConflictError extends APIError {}
export class PayloadTooLargeError extends APIError {}

// in fromResponse, before the 5xx arm:
if (status === 402) return new PaymentRequiredError(status, body, headers)
if (status === 409) return new ConflictError(status, body, headers)
if (status === 413) return new PayloadTooLargeError(status, body, headers)
```

plus the corresponding exports from `src/index.ts`.

## Reproduction without an API key

The mapping is a pure function, so the assertions above run offline — no credential
and no network. `test/errors.test.ts` already covers this area and is the natural
place for the three new cases.

## Environment

`@typesafe-ai/sdk` 0.6.0. Verified against the installed package's own exports, by
calling `APIError.fromResponse` directly.

## Note

If `409` is not a status this API emits — the docs mention it for conflicts, but I
have not seen one — then leaving it on the base class is defensible, and only `402`
and `413` need classes. I have not been able to trigger a real `402`, since that
would require exhausting a balance.

title: score() accepts a null level that the API refuses with 422, and the docs list null as an accepted shape
body:
## Summary

`ScoreCriteria` accepts `null` levels at the type level, and the docs say a level
description may be `null`, but `POST /v1/systemone` refuses one with `422`. A `null`
level cannot be sent at all, and because a level's position *is* its score, silently
dropping it would renumber the scale — so an integrator following the docs has no
correct move.

## What the docs and types say

[Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced) lists where JSON
structure is allowed:

| Field | Applies to | Accepted shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `criteria` entries (level descriptions) | Score | `string`, `object`, `array`, or `null` |

and `src/questions.ts` types it the same way, since `EntryType` includes `null`:

```ts
type EntryType = string | { [key: string]: JsonValue } | JsonValue[] | null
type ScoreCriteria = readonly [EntryType, EntryType, ...EntryType[]]
```

## What the API actually does

Verified today against `api.typesafe.ai` on `jev-1.13.0`.

**A `null` level is refused:**

```sh
curl -sS -X POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"state":"The disk is 99% full and writes are failing.","model":"jev-latest",
       "questions":{"severity":{"type":"score","instructions":"How severe?",
       "criteria":["none",null,"severe"]}}}'
```

```
HTTP 422
{"detail":[{"type":"string_type","loc":["body","questions","severity","score","criteria",1,"str"],
            "msg":"Input should be a valid string","input":null},
           {"type":"dict_type","loc":["body","questions","severity","score","criteria",1,"dict[any,any]"],
            "msg":"Input should be a valid dictionary","input":null}]}
```

**The other documented shapes are accepted**, so only `null` is at issue:

| `criteria` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `["none","severe"]` | `200` |
| `["none",{"what":"degraded"},"severe"]` | `200`, and the `legend` returns the object |
| `["none","","severe"]` | `200`, `legend` `{"0":"none","1":"","2":"severe"}` |
| `["none",null,"severe"]` | **`422`** |

## Why this is worth fixing rather than documenting away

A level's position in `criteria` **is** its score — the [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score)
page says the levels are "an ordered array of level descriptions, from the low end
of the scale to the high end", and the migration guide notes you can no longer skip
levels. So a caller who wants level 1 to exist but not be described has three
options, and only one works:

1. send `null` → `422`, per above;
2. drop the entry → the rubric silently becomes 2 levels, `"severe"` moves from
   position 2 to position 1, and every answer's `legend` maps back to the wrong
   name. This is the worse outcome, because it succeeds;
3. send `""` → accepted, position preserved.

Option 3 is a fine workaround, but nothing documents it, and `null` is what both the
docs and the types advertise.

## Suggested fix

Either:

- **document `""`** as the way to hold an undescribed position, and drop `null` from
  the accepted-shapes table for Score `criteria` entries (and from `ScoreCriteria`
  via `EntryType`); or
- **accept `null`** on the wire and treat it as an empty description, which is what
  the docs and the type currently promise.

Either way, a test would pin it. `score('How severe?', ['none', null, 'severe'])`
currently builds and returns `["none",null,"severe"]`, and sending exactly that
payload is what produces the 422 above — the same shape of gap as #6, where the
SDK's own builder accepts something its API refuses.

## Verified end to end

```js
const q = sdk.score('How severe?', ['none', null, 'severe'])
// q.criteria -> ["none", null, "severe"]
await client.systemOne({ state: 'Disk 99% full.', questions: { severity: q } })
// -> 422 questions.severity.score.criteria.1.str: Input should be a valid string
```

So the SDK accepts the value, forwards it unchanged, and the API rejects it. Nothing
in between warns the caller.

## Environment

- `@typesafe-ai/sdk` 0.6.0 (types read from `dist/index.d.mts`)
- `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`, model `jev-latest` → `jev-1.13.0`
- Found while writing an integration against the documented shapes; the surrounding
  audit is at https://github.com/PerryLink/jevcore if it is useful context.

title: Feature: calibrated multi-label selection (Choice is single-select; multi-label needs ad-hoc distribution thresholds)
body:
## Summary

Add first-class support for **calibrated multi-label selection** — a task where more than one option legitimately applies and you want a calibrated cutoff, not an argmax.

## Motivation / real use case

Mapping a security detection rule to MITRE ATT&CK: a single rule frequently maps to several techniques at once (execution + persistence + a discovery behavior). We tried the documented primitives:

- **One `noul` per technique**: independent judgments don't compete, so a broad rule lights up 10-15 "yes" answers (blowout), and confusable neighbors (e.g. recon vs discovery) both fire because nothing forces a choice between them.
- **One `score` per technique**: same problem — per-item scores are still independent, so neighbors don't separate.
- **A single `choice` over the candidate techniques**: this *does* make them compete (the normalized distribution correctly suppresses the weaker neighbor), which is what we wanted — but `choice` is single-select. To get a multi-label set we read the full `probabilities` and apply ad-hoc relative thresholds (keep options with `p >= 0.10 AND p >= 0.25 * max`). Those cutoffs are hand-tuned and uncalibrated.

## What would help

A primitive (or documented, calibrated pattern) for "select the set of options that apply" from a competitive/normalized distribution — i.e. the competition behavior of `choice` combined with a principled, calibrated inclusion boundary instead of a magic-number relative threshold. Essentially: `noul`'s calibration, but competitive across a labeled option set.

If this is already achievable via an existing pattern we missed, a cookbook entry for competitive multi-label selection would be very welcome.

title: Feature: reuse/cache identical criteria across requests (prompt caching or registered questions) + expose cached_tokens
body:
## Summary

Provide a way to avoid re-sending (and re-billing) identical `criteria` across many `systemOne` requests — e.g. automatic server-side prompt caching keyed on the criteria, a register-once "question template" referenced by id, or client-side reuse of a compiled question — and expose cache hits via a `cached_tokens` field on `Usage`.

## Motivation / real use case

We're using System One (Jev) to map security detection rules to the MITRE ATT&CK v19 taxonomy. The classification runs over a **fixed taxonomy**: ~222 techniques and ~475 sub-techniques, each option seeded with its MITRE definition so the model can discriminate confusable neighbors. That criteria block is **byte-identical on every request** — only the `state` (the rule under analysis) changes.

We measured that the definitions are **load-bearing, not padding**: dropping them to bare option names collapses discrimination (a "network service discovery vs active scanning" pair inverts — the wrong neighbor wins — and a signed-binary-proxy technique drops out of the candidate set entirely). So we can't trim them for quality reasons. But re-sending the same ~6k tokens of definitions on every rule across a library of thousands of rules is pure redundant input.

Per-call cost is tiny, so this isn't urgent for us — but for high-volume, fixed-taxonomy classification (a canonical System One shape) it's a lot of repeated input tokens with zero information change between calls.

## What would help (any one of)

1. **Automatic server-side prompt caching** keyed on a hash of the `criteria` (and/or instructions), transparent to the caller, with hits reported as `cached_tokens` in `Usage`.
2. **Register-once questions**: create a question/criteria definition, get an id, and pass `{ questionId }` (plus per-call overrides) on subsequent requests instead of the full inline `criteria`.
3. **Client-side compiled/reusable questions** in the SDK that keep the wire payload small.

## Observability

Regardless of the mechanism, adding `cached_tokens` (or `cache_read_tokens`) to the `Usage` interface would let callers measure the effect. Today `Usage` exposes only `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` (v0.6.0).

Happy to share more detail on the workload if useful.

title: Blank Retry-After headers bypass configured backoff and retry immediately
body:
## Summary

At `66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214`, a present but empty or whitespace-only `Retry-After` (or `retry-after-ms`) header is parsed as a valid zero delay. The public retry path then bypasses the configured fallback backoff.

## Expected behavior

`parseRetryAfter` documents that invalid/garbage values return `undefined`, allowing `retryDelayMs` to use policy backoff. Literal `Retry-After: 0` remains a valid explicit zero delay.

## Actual behavior

JavaScript `Number("")` and `Number("   ")` return `0`. The parser checks finiteness/non-negativity after conversion without first rejecting empty syntax, so malformed headers become immediate-retry instructions.

## Reproduction

```sh
node repros/js-sdk-blank-retry-after-parent.mjs red
```

The public `TypeSafeClient.models.list()` path receives a 503 with whitespace-only `Retry-After`, using a deterministic 200ms/no-jitter retry policy. Three repetitions exited 1:

```text
AssertionError: whitespace-only Retry-After was treated as zero and retried after 18.6ms
AssertionError: whitespace-only Retry-After was treated as zero and retried after 20.5ms
AssertionError: whitespace-only Retry-After was treated as zero and retried after 19.2ms
```

Control:

```sh
node repros/js-sdk-blank-retry-after-parent.mjs control
# CONTROL: absent Retry-After used configured 200ms backoff (225.1ms)
```

The transport is fully in-memory; no external request is made.

## Impact

A malformed server or intermediary header can bypass a caller's configured backoff and trigger immediate retries. This audit did not test a live rate-limit incident.

## Root cause

`src/retry.ts:38-47` numerically converts header text before validating that it contains a numeric or HTTP-date value.

## Suggested fix and regression test

Trim and reject empty strings before numeric parsing for both header variants, while preserving literal zero and valid dates. Add public retry-path tests for absent, blank, whitespace, literal zero, valid seconds/date, and malformed values under deterministic backoff.

## Duplicate check

The complete issue/comment/timeline corpus was inspected; no PR history or open PR is exposed. Fresh searches covered the exact symptom, `parseRetryAfter`, `src/retry.ts`, immediate retry, `Number(raw)`, empty/malformed header terminology, backoff, and organization-wide `retry-after-ms` synonyms. No prior mention was found.

title: Accepted timeouts above Node's timer maximum fire after about 1ms
body:
## Summary

At `66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214`, `TypeSafeClient` accepts `timeout: 2147483648` as a positive finite millisecond timeout, but Node clamps it to 1ms. The request then fails almost immediately with `APITimeoutError`.

## Expected behavior

The public option is a per-attempt duration in milliseconds. Accepted timeout values should either represent that duration or be rejected clearly.

## Actual behavior

`assertPositiveMs` accepts every positive finite number. The value is passed directly to `setTimeout`; Node's signed 32-bit timer boundary emits `TimeoutOverflowWarning` and sets the delay to 1ms.

## Reproduction

```sh
node repros/js-sdk-timeout-overflow-parent.mjs red
```

Three repetitions exited 1. Observed durations were 1.2–1.4ms:

```text
TimeoutOverflowWarning: 2147483648 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer.
Timeout duration was set to 1.
AssertionError: configured timeout 2147483648ms fired after only 1.3ms
```

Control:

```sh
node repros/js-sdk-timeout-overflow-parent.mjs control
# CONTROL: 40ms timeout fired after 44.3ms
```

The fetch implementation is a local in-memory hanging transport; no network request is made.

## Impact

A caller requesting a long but accepted deadline receives a near-immediate timeout. This was tested on Node 22.23.1; browser and alternative runtime behavior was not tested.

## Root cause

- `src/client.ts:77-84` validates positivity/finiteness but not the runtime timer bound.
- `src/client.ts:419-422` passes the accepted value directly to `setTimeout`.

## Suggested fix and regression test

Reject unsupported values above the runtime timer maximum, or implement a safely chunked long timer. Apply the rule to both constructor and per-call overrides. Test `2^31-1`, `2^31`, ordinary values, and non-finite values.

## Duplicate check

All available issues/comments/timelines were inspected; the repository has no accessible PR history or open PR. Fresh searches covered the exact warning, numeric boundary, `setTimeout`, large/32-bit timeout terms, validation wording, clamp terminology, and organization-wide synonyms. No prior mention was found.

title: Community Go SDK — would you consider listing third-party clients in the docs?
body:
The docs [SDK page](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk) lists Python and JavaScript, and otherwise points people at the raw HTTP API. There is no Go client, so I wrote one:

**https://github.com/Tangerg/typesafe-sdk-go**

```sh
go get github.com/Tangerg/typesafe-sdk-go
```

```go
client, err := typesafe.NewClient(nil) // reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY

result, err := client.SystemOne(ctx, &typesafe.SystemOneRequest{
    State: "I was charged twice. Please fix this ASAP.",
    Questions: typesafe.Questions{
        "category": &typesafe.ChoiceQuestion{
            Instructions: "What is this ticket about?",
            Criteria: typesafe.ChoiceCriteria{"billing": nil, "technical": nil, "other": nil},
        },
    },
}, nil)

category, err := result.Answers.Choice("category")
fmt.Println(category.Choice, category.Probability(), category.Confidence)
```

It covers `POST /v1/systemone` with all three primitives and `GET /v1/models`, and matches the behavior your own SDKs document: the same headers including `X-TypeSafe-Retry-Count`, the same default retry policy (408, 429 and 5xx plus connection failures and timeouts, exponential backoff from 500ms to 5s with 25% jitter, `Retry-After` honored up to a minute), and the same error-message extraction from `detail` / `error` / `message` bodies. MIT, no third-party dependencies, Go 1.25+.

Where Go has a better answer than a direct transliteration, it takes it — `context.Context` instead of an `AbortSignal`, `errors.Is` against error-class sentinels instead of `instanceof`, structs instead of question builders — and each of those choices is written down in the README.

It is tested two ways. Unit tests run offline against response payloads captured from the live API. Integration tests behind a build tag call the real service and check each documented limit **from both sides**: that 10 score levels and 255 choice labels are accepted, and that 11 and 256 are still refused. If you relax a limit, my tests fail and tell me to catch up, rather than leaving the SDK stricter than the API. Those tests are where the findings in #6 came from.

**The ask:** if you would like third-party clients listed, a "Community" line on the SDK page pointing here would help Go users find it. If you would rather keep that page to official SDKs only, that is completely reasonable — please just close this.

To be clear about what it is: a community project, not affiliated with or endorsed by TypeSafe, and the README and NOTICE both say so. I am not asking you to adopt or maintain it. If you do build an official Go SDK later, I am happy to point people at it.

title: v0.6.0 can build two request shapes the API rejects: noul() with no arguments, and state: null
body:
Both of these type-check, are asserted by the test suite, and are refused by `api.typesafe.ai`. Verified against the live API today on `jev-latest` with v0.6.0.

## 1. `noul()` with no instructions

`noul()` defaults `instructions` to `null` ([`src/questions.ts`](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/main/src/questions.ts)), which serializes to `{"type":"noul","instructions":null}`.

```
POST /v1/systemone
{"model":"jev-latest","state":"s","questions":{"q":{"type":"noul","instructions":null}}}

400 {"detail":"Noul question must have criteria or instructions: q"}
```

The API's rule is that a noul needs **at least one of** `instructions` or `criteria`. Criteria alone is accepted:

```
{"type":"noul","instructions":null,"criteria":{"true":"it is a greeting","false":"it is not"}}   → 200
{"type":"noul","instructions":null,"criteria":{}}                                                → 400
{"type":"noul","instructions":null,"criteria":{"true":null,"false":null}}                        → 400
```

So an empty criteria object, and one whose sides are both `null`, count as no criteria.

`test/client.test.ts:344` asserts `defaultInstructions: noul()` is sent as `{ type: "noul", instructions: null }`, so the suite currently pins a request the API will refuse.

## 2. `state: null`

`SystemOneRequest.state` is typed `EntryType`, which includes `null` ([`src/types.ts:11`](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/main/src/types.ts), `:162`).

```
POST /v1/systemone
{"model":"jev-latest","state":null,"questions":{"q":{"type":"noul","instructions":"x"}}}

422 {"detail":[{"type":"missing","loc":["body","state"],"msg":"Field required","input":{...}}]}
```

`test/client.test.ts:333` asserts `state: null` is sent through unchanged.

Empty values *are* accepted, so it is only `null` that is refused:

| state | |
| --- | --- |
| `""` | 200 |
| `{}` | 200 |
| `[]` | 200 |
| `null` | 422 |
| `42` | 422 (`string_type` / `dict_type` / `list_type`) |

Narrowing `SystemOneRequest["state"]` to exclude `null` would catch this at compile time.

## Two limits the SDK does not check

The primitives docs state them, and the API enforces them, but `validateQuestions` only checks the score minimum:

```
score criteria, 11 levels  → 400 {"detail":"Too many score levels. Must have at most 10 levels."}
choice criteria, 256 labels → 400 {"detail":"Too many choices. Must have at most 255 choices."}
```

10 levels and 255 labels are both accepted, so the bounds are 2–10 and 1–255. A single-label choice is fine and comes back with `confidence: 1.0`.

## One rule I could not find documented

An empty question key is refused:

```
{"questions":{"":{"type":"noul","instructions":"x"}}}  → 400 {"detail":"Question key cannot be empty."}
```

A whitespace-only key such as `"   "` is accepted, so the check is on the empty string exactly.

## Docs note

[primitives/noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul) says `instructions` is required. Given finding 1, "instructions or criteria is required" would match the API. [concepts/state](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state) does not mention that `null` is refused while `""`, `{}` and `[]` are accepted.

---

Happy to open these as separate issues if that suits your triage better. I understand PRs are not being accepted yet, so this is a report rather than a patch.

title: Numeric choice labels are inferred as never instead of their JSON string labels
body:
## Summary

`choice(null, { 0: null, 1: null })` is accepted by the public TypeScript API and serializes identically to `choice(null, { "0": null, "1": null })`. However, the former produces `ResultFor<typeof question>["choice"] = never`, while the latter correctly produces `"0" | "1"`.

This is a type-inference defect, not a request serialization failure or a claim about API answer quality.

## Affected commit / version and environment

- `main`: `66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214`, also tagged `v0.6.0`.
- Tested source, clean local build, and actual npm `@typesafe-ai/sdk@0.6.0` package.
- Local and published package tarballs were byte-identical.
- Node 22.23.1, TypeScript 7.0.2, Linux x86_64 / WSL2.
- Source type tests: Vitest 4.1.11; locked project installation used npm 11.19.0. Independent consumer installation used npm 10.9.8.
- Both ESM `.d.mts` and CommonJS `.d.cts` package declarations reproduced the issue.
- Older SDK releases and other compiler versions were not tested.

## Supported user workflow

Construct a choice question with numeric-looking labels, then consume the inferred selected-label type. Numeric object-literal property names satisfy the exported `ChoiceCriteria` constraint. JSON transports these keys as strings; quoting the same keys should not change the answer type.

## Expected behavior and supporting reference

Infer `"0" | "1"` for the selected label, matching the wire keys and the quoted-key control.

Version-pinned contract:

- [README: answer types are inferred from questions](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214/README.md#L33).
- [ChoiceCriteria and ChoiceQuestion](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214/src/types.ts#L34-L46).
- [choice builder: labels mapped to descriptions](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214/src/questions.ts#L49-L63).
- [ResultFor: preserving criteria keys](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214/src/types.ts#L117-L124).

No explicit numeric-label exclusion was found. The compiler accepts the question itself; the failure arises from its inferred answer type.

## Minimal reproduction

In a fresh consumer directory:

```sh
npm init -y
npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund @typesafe-ai/sdk@0.6.0
npm install --save-dev --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund typescript@7.0.2
```

Save `numeric.mts`:

```ts
import { choice, type ResultFor } from '@typesafe-ai/sdk';
const question = choice(null, { 0: null, 1: null });
const selected: ResultFor<typeof question>['choice'] = '0';
```

Passing control, `control.mts`:

```ts
import { choice, type ResultFor } from '@typesafe-ai/sdk';
const question = choice(null, { '0': null, '1': null });
const selected: ResultFor<typeof question>['choice'] = '0';
```

From that consumer directory:

```sh
node_modules/.bin/tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --strict --target ES2022 --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext numeric.mts
node_modules/.bin/tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --strict --target ES2022 --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext control.mts
```

The audit used the checkout's locked TypeScript 7.0.2 executable against an independent installed consumer, with these exact compiler flags and network access disabled. The numeric probe exited 1 and the positive control exited 0. Both were rerun before filing with identical results. Both `.cts` variants were also tested against local and published packages.

No `any`, type assertion, suppressed compiler error, or mock compiler is involved.

## Observed output

```text
numeric.mts(3,7): error TS2322: Type '"0"' is not assignable to type 'never'.
```

The quoted-key control compiles successfully.

The source-level regression below produced **1 failed / 2 passed**; the same result was obtained in a fresh process. Separate runtime assertions through `systemOne` verified that numeric and quoted-key spellings produce identical JSON request bodies and return the same synthetic string-labeled response. That fixture validates SDK transport/type consistency, not live API behavior.

## Minimal regression test

Save as `test/numeric-choice.test-d.ts` in the source checkout:

```ts
import { expectTypeOf, test } from 'vitest';
import { choice, score, type ResultFor } from '../src';

test('string label control preserves labels', () => {
  const question = choice(null, { '0': null, '1': null });
  expectTypeOf<ResultFor<typeof question>['choice']>().toEqualTypeOf<'0' | '1'>();
});

test('numeric label spelling preserves the JSON wire labels', () => {
  const question = choice(null, { 0: null, 1: null });
  expectTypeOf<ResultFor<typeof question>['choice']>().toEqualTypeOf<'0' | '1'>();
});

test('JSON array descriptions preserve choice labels and score indices', () => {
  const selected = choice(null, { yes: ['example'], no: null });
  expectTypeOf<ResultFor<typeof selected>['choice']>().toEqualTypeOf<'yes' | 'no'>();
  const scored = score(null, [['low'], null]);
  expectTypeOf<keyof ResultFor<typeof scored>['probabilities']>().toEqualTypeOf<'0' | '1'>();
});
```

Run from the repository root after installing the locked dependencies:

```sh
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --typecheck.only test/numeric-choice.test-d.ts
```

This is the executed regression, with its audit-only filename changed for presentation.

## Root cause

[ChoiceResponse.choice](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214/src/types.ts#L79-L89) uses:

```ts
readonly choice: keyof T & string;
```

For numeric literal properties, `keyof T` is `0 | 1`. Intersecting it with `string` removes all labels instead of representing their JSON string spelling.

The [builder](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214/src/questions.ts#L55-L63) accepts the map unchanged, and [systemOne](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/66880ccded6cb642dc1809620c2b108c33730214/src/client.ts#L311-L324) forwards it. This is not an import-resolution, stale-build, or missing-dependency failure.

## Confirmed impact, severity and workaround

**Low severity:** consumers using numeric literal property names cannot represent a valid selected label with the inferred type, which becomes `never`. The underlying JSON request is unchanged; no runtime data loss, server rejection, or incorrect model output is claimed.

Workaround: quote numeric-looking keys, e.g. `{ "0": null, "1": null }`. Ordinary alphabetic labels and the basic SDK call are not blocked.

## Duplicate research

Before filing, current main was checked and remains at the SHA above. All public SDK issues and PRs were enumerated in all states. Existing issue #2 and PR #3 concern native-fetch cancellation; PR #1 concerns bootstrap publishing. None covers this inference problem; PR #3 explicitly excludes numeric choice inference.

All-state searches included `"choice" "numeric"`, `never`, and `keyof`. Source history (`git log -p -- src/types.ts`) and the changelog were also inspected. No matching public report or intentional numeric-label exclusion was found. This is not a claim about private tracker contents or absolute originality.

## Suggested fix direction

Represent supported string/number criteria keys using their JSON string-label spelling rather than filtering numeric keys out. Check consistency with probability-map keys and mixed string/numeric maps, preserve ordinary string unions, and test both source and emitted declarations. No fix is included in this report.
